newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN POLICE NET TWO WHITES AFTER THREE BLASTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN POLICE NET TWO WHITES AFTER THREE BLASTS.

text.p: Two white men have been arrested by South African police in connection with three bomb blasts which exploded at a mosque, post office and shop north west of Johannesburg early on Sunday.

The blasts occurred between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. (2300 GMT and 0100 GMT) at and around the traditionally conservative town of Rustenburg in North West region. Two black men who were sleeping at the mosque were slightly hurt in the one blast.
"Police have made two arrests during the course of this morning. They are two white men and they will taken in for questioning at this stage," police Captain Belinda Kleynhans told Reuters.
The men were arrested in Mooi Nooi, a small platinum mining town outside Rustenburg, Kleynhans said.

She said detectives from the Bomb Squad were investigating the blasts, but were as yet unable to identify the type of explosive devices used. Fragments were being collected and would be sent off for tests, she added.

The mosque blast was the first one to rip through Rustenburg's Ziniaville suburb. The injured men were apparently only bruised and were sleeping on the premises to guard the mosque. Damage of 250,000 rand (($53,200) was caused.
Kleynhans said the second explosion was at the Marikana post office some 40 kilometres (25 miles) from Rustenburg. Damage was also calculated at 250,000 rand.

The third blast took place at a small wholsesaler's shop called On The Bent at Olifantsnek just outside Rustenberg and damage was estimated at 120,000 rand, Kleynhans said. Police were still investigating a possible motive, she added.
South African police are also probing a Christmas Eve bomb attack that killed four people in a small farming town.

An unknown white right-wing group called the Boere Attack Troop (BAT) has claimed resposibility for the twin pipe bomb attack at a supermarket and pharmacy in Worcester, 90 km (55 miles) northeast of Cape Town.
One adult and three children were killed and about 60 people wounded in the attack. Most of the casualties were blacks or of mixed-race descent.
